components.name: Nadir Multi-Band Imager (NMI-10)
components.description: Compact visible-light pushbroom optical camera designed for small satellites and CubeSats.

trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Trades ground resolution for low mass, modest data rate, and low pointing requirements.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Planet Labs Dove Classic Imager / ECSS-E-ST-10C
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Calibrated against commercial 3U-6U CubeSat imaging payloads.

components.name: High-Resolution Panchromatic Telescope (HRPT-02)
components.description: Ritchey-Chrétien optical telescope with Time Delay Integration (TDI) CCD sensor for sub-meter Earth observation.

disadvantages: Extreme data generation requiring dedicated X/Ka comms
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Yields high science score but demands major bus mass, large reaction wheels, and rapid downlink capacity.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Airbus NAOMI / SPOT-6 Instrument / NASA Landsat-8 OLI benchmark
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Based on modern 50-70 kg small-satellite optical observation systems.

components.name: Phased Array Synthetic Aperture Radar (ARES-SAR)
components.description: Active C-band phased array radar providing all-weather day/night surface deformation and topography mapping.

advantages: Operates through clouds, dust, and nighttime
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Provides uncompromised all-weather radar data but requires heavy class bus, large battery pack, and dedicated radiators.

reference_source.heritage_reference: ESA Sentinel-1 SAR / ICEYE X-band SAR array
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Scaled down from 800 kg bus systems to a modern 185 kg small-sat SAR benchmark.

components.name: Fluxgate Vector Magnetometer (FVM-01)
components.description: Precision tri-axial fluxgate magnetometer mounted on a deployable boom to measure planetary and space weather magnetic fields.

trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Cheap and light science score booster, but adds single-point mechanical boom deployment risk.

reference_source.heritage_reference: NASA THEMIS / Juno MAG / Cassini Magnetometer
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard NASA JPL space-physics instrument payload.

components.name: Body-Mounted Silicon Solar Array (BM-Si-40)
components.description: High-durability crystalline silicon solar cells adhered directly to exterior structural bus panels.

disadvantages: Generation drops when spacecraft yaws or rolls away from Sun
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Eliminates deployment failure risk at the cost of requiring whole-spacecraft sun-pointing.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Standard 12U CubeSat Body Panels / ECSS-E-ST-20C
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Assumes standard Earth orbit 1 AU solar constant.

components.name: Deployable GaAs Triple-Junction Solar Wings (DW-GaAs-350)
components.description: Deployable fold-out solar panel wings utilizing InGaP/InGaAs/Ge triple-junction solar cells.

disadvantages: Increases aerodynamic drag area in LEO
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Provides ample power for multi-sensor payloads while increasing orbital drag and deployment complexity.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Spectrolab NeXt Triple Junction (XTJ) Arrays / NASA SMD benchmarks
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Widely deployed across NASA and commercial small-sat buses.

components.name: Articulated Sun-Tracking Solar Array (ASTA-1800)
components.description: Dual-wing solar array equipped with Solar Array Drive Mechanisms (SADM) for continuous 360-degree solar tracking.

advantages: Massive 1.85 kW generation supports SAR or Ion engines
disadvantages: Complex motorized slip rings with wear life limits
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Maximum power generation decoupling spacecraft attitude from solar orientation, paid for in mass and mechanical risk.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Lockheed Martin LM-2100 / Maxar 1300 SADM architectures
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard aerospace high-power satellite bus mechanism.

components.name: Standard LiFePO4 Energy Module (BATT-120)
components.description: Lithium Iron Phosphate battery pack with integrated cell-balancing charge regulator.

advantages: Chemically stable with zero thermal runaway risk
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Trades mass efficiency for chemical safety and resilience against overcharging.

reference_source.heritage_reference: GomSpace NanoPower P-series / ECSS-E-ST-20-30C
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Proven small-satellite battery standard.

components.name: Aerospace Li-Ion Spacecraft Cell Pack (BATT-750)
components.description: Space-qualified 18650 NMC Lithium-Ion battery module with thermal heaters and cell isolation switches.

disadvantages: Requires active thermal management (must be kept between 0°C and 25°C)
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: High energy storage per kg but requires dedicated heater power to avoid electrolyte freezing in eclipse.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Saft VES-16 / ABSL Space Products Li-ion Batteries
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard NASA/ESA LEO Earth observation battery system.

components.name: Solid-State High-Discharge Power System (BATT-3000)
components.description: Next-generation solid-state lithium ceramic battery pack designed for massive pulsed loads (SAR, high-thrust electric propulsion).

trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Enables power-hungry radar instruments and long planetary occultations, but consumes a large fraction of mission budget.

reference_source.heritage_reference: NASA ARPA-E Solid-State Aviation/Space Battery prototypes
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Represents emerging solid-state aerospace battery flight demos.

components.name: Omnidirectional S-Band Patch Antenna (S-OMNI-01)
components.description: Dual-patch microstrip antenna providing hemispherical coverage for low-rate telemetry, tracking, and command (TT&C).

advantages: Wide beamwidth allows communication during spacecraft tumbling or emergency safe mode
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Guarantees command link survival during emergencies, but acts as a bottleneck for science data.

reference_source.heritage_reference: EnduroSat S-Band Patch / ECSS-E-ST-50-05C
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard emergency and housekeeping TT&C antenna.

components.name: Medium-Gain X-Band Horn Antenna (X-HORN-02)
components.description: Conical horn antenna paired with an 8-Watt solid-state power amplifier (SSPA) for high-rate Earth observation downlink.

advantages: 120 Mbps enables dumping tens of gigabytes during a single 8-minute ground station pass
disadvantages: Requires spacecraft to slew nadir-offset toward ground station during passes
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: High data throughput without a mechanical gimbal, requiring the whole spacecraft to point at the ground station.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Syrlinks EWC27 X-Band Transmitter / NASA Earth Observing-1
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Widely utilized in commercial LEO imaging constellations.

components.name: Gimbaled Ka-Band Parabolic Reflector (KA-DISH-03)
components.description: 0.75-meter carbon-composite parabolic dish on a 2-axis pointing gimbal paired with a 25W Ka-Band Traveling Wave Tube Amplifier (TWTA).

advantages: Downlinks simultaneously while instruments observe (via 2-axis gimbal)
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Eliminates data bottleneck entirely, but introduces mechanical gimbal vibration and heavy pointing demands on ADCS.

reference_source.heritage_reference: NASA Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Ka-Band Dish / Inmarsat-5
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard for high-throughput lunar and Earth observation missions.

components.name: Standard Flight Computer (LEON3-FT-01)
components.description: Fault-tolerant SPARC V8 32-bit processor running RTEMS real-time operating system with SpaceWire and CAN bus interfaces.

advantages: Extensive flight heritage across ESA missions
disadvantages: Cannot execute onboard AI or image compression
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Provides reliable housekeeping and fault management, but cannot process high-rate science data in real time.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Cobham Gaisler UT699 LEON3-FT / ESA PROBA-2
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Core European space flight computer.

components.name: Rad-Hard PowerPC Command & Control (RAD750-02)
components.description: Radiation-hardened PowerPC 750 processor enclosed in a structural aluminum chassis with redundant MIL-STD-1553B interfaces.

advantages: Immune to single-event latchups up to 200 krad
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Offers high radiation resilience for deep-space and high-altitude missions, but adds cost and mass.

reference_source.heritage_reference: BAE Systems RAD750 / NASA Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter & Kepler
reference_source.benchmark_notes: NASA flagship mission computing standard.

components.name: Heterogeneous Space Edge Processor (HSEP-AI-03)
components.description: Quad-core ARM Cortex-R5 with radiation-mitigated Neural Processing Unit (NPU) accelerator for onboard cloud filtering and data compression.

advantages: 4.5x data compression reduces downlink demand by 75%
disadvantages: Generates significant waste heat requiring thermal radiators
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Reduces required downlink bandwidth via onboard AI data compression, but demands additional power and thermal cooling.

reference_source.heritage_reference: ESA PhiSat-1 Intel Movidius Myriad 2 / KP Labs Leopard DPU
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Represents modern edge-computing smallsat developments.

components.name: Cold Gas Reaction Control Thruster (CG-RCS-01)
components.description: Pressurized dry nitrogen cold gas propulsion system with 4 canted micro-nozzles for attitude detumbling and orbit trimming.

advantages: Simple pressurized gas system with high reliability
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Provides reliable attitude detumbling with zero toxicity risk, but lacks the Delta-V needed for major orbit maneuvers.

reference_source.heritage_reference: VACCO Cold Gas Propulsion System / MarCO Mars CubeSats
reference_source.benchmark_notes: NASA JPL MarCO flyby mission heritage.

components.name: Hydrazine Monopropellant System (MONO-HYD-02)
components.description: Catalytic hydrazine decomposition propulsion module featuring a titanium propellant tank with an elastomeric diaphragm.

advantages: High thrust (22 N) executes rapid orbital changes
disadvantages: Toxic propellant requires specialized ground-handling procedures
Propellant lines require continuous freeze protection heaters
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Delivers substantial Delta-V for orbital adjustments and deorbiting, but requires active thermal heater management.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Aerojet Rocketdyne MR-106 / Moog Monopropellant Systems
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard aerospace orbital stationkeeping propulsion.

components.name: Xenon Hall-Effect Electric Propulsion (HALL-XEN-03)
components.description: High-efficiency Hall-effect plasma thruster with magnetic shielding and a carbon-composite xenon propellant tank.

disadvantages: Tiny thrust (65 mN) requires days of continuous burning
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Enables orbit raising and interplanetary transfers with minimal propellant mass, but requires a high-capacity power subsystem.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Busek BHT-600 / Safran PPS-1350 / Starlink Krypton/Xenon Hall thrusters
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Modern high-efficiency orbital propulsion benchmark.

components.name: Coarse Magnetorquer Rod Triad (MT-ROD-01)
components.description: Three orthogonal magnetic torque rods that interact with planetary magnetic fields to provide 3-axis desaturation.

advantages: Zero moving parts with virtually zero wear
Uses zero propellant to dump momentum
disadvantages: Only functions within planetary magnetic fields (useless in deep space/GEO)
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Provides propellant-free attitude detumbling in LEO, but cannot satisfy precision pointing requirements.

reference_source.heritage_reference: ZARM Technik Magnetorquers / NewSpace Systems MT
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard LEO satellite attitude desaturation hardware.

components.name: Reaction Wheel Array with Sun Sensors (RWA-SUN-02)
components.description: Tetrahedral array of 4 reaction wheels with digital sun sensors and MEMS rate gyros for 3-axis stabilization.

advantages: Slew rate of 1.5 deg/sec allows target tracking
disadvantages: Reaction wheels saturate from disturbance torques and require periodic desaturation
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Delivers the pointing precision required for imaging payloads, but needs thrusters or magnetorquers to periodically dump momentum.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Collins Aerospace / Honeywell HR0610 Reaction Wheels
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard Earth observation smallsat reaction wheel assembly.

components.name: Precision Star Tracker & CMG Suite (ST-CMG-03)
components.description: Dual optical star trackers paired with Control Moment Gyroscopes (CMG) and fiber-optic gyroscopes for high-agility pointing.

advantages: Rapid slewing allows multiple targets per orbit pass
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Unlocks high-resolution optical and planetary instruments, but demands significant mass, power, and budget.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Terma HE-5AS Star Tracker / Honeywell Miniature CMGs / WorldView-3
reference_source.benchmark_notes: High-agility commercial Earth observation benchmark.

components.name: Passive MLI & Thermal Coating Kit (MLI-COAT-01)
components.description: Multi-Layer Insulation (MLI) blankets composed of aluminized Mylar with high-emissivity black anodized exterior radiator surfaces.

disadvantages: Fixed thermal dissipation cannot adjust to changing power profiles or deep eclipses
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Provides maintenance-free passive thermal stabilization, but lacks the ability to adjust to variable internal thermal loads.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Sheldahl Aerospace MLI Blankets / ECSS-E-ST-31C
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Foundational satellite thermal control system.

components.name: Heat Pipe Loop with Survival Heaters (HPIPE-HEAT-02)
components.description: Ammonia Constant Conductance Heat Pipes (CCHP) coupled with thermostatically controlled electric survival heaters.

advantages: Transports internal heat directly to external radiators
Prevents battery freezing during extended eclipses
disadvantages: Consumes 28 W of battery energy for survival heaters during night passes
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Maintains tight component temperatures across variable orbits, but increases nighttime battery drain.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Advanced Cooling Technologies (ACT) Space CCHP / NASA GPM
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard intermediate spacecraft thermal control architecture.

components.name: Active Stirling Cryocooler & Louver Radiator (CRYO-LOUV-03)
components.description: Miniature pulse-tube Stirling cryocooler paired with bimetallic thermal louvers for sub-80K sensor cooling and dynamic heat rejection.

advantages: Cools infrared and radar focal planes below 80 K to suppress thermal noise
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Required for infrared sensors, but introduces micro-vibrations and increases the bus power budget.

reference_source.heritage_reference: AIM Infrarot-Module Stirling Cryocoolers / NASA James Webb MIRI cooler
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Cryogenic thermal control benchmark for high-performance space payloads.

components.name: 12U Standard CubeSat Chassis (12U-STR-ALU)
components.description: Precision-machined Aerospace 6061-T6 aluminum chassis conforming to standard CubeSat dispenser deployer specifications.

advantages: Standardized deployer interface fits low-cost rideshare slots
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Enables affordable rideshare access to orbit, but limits payload mass, volume, and aperture size.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Pumpkin Inc. / NanoRacks 12U Deployer Specification / AIAA S-120
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standardized small-satellite form-factor.

components.name: Composite Hexagonal SmallSat Bus (HEX-CFRP-02)
components.description: Hexagonal carbon fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) bus with aluminum honeycomb core shear webs and ESPA ring bolt interfaces.

advantages: Near-zero coefficient of thermal expansion keeps optical sensors aligned
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Minimizes structural mass while maintaining optical alignment, but costs significantly more than machined aluminum.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Moog ESPA-ring SmallSat Chassis / Surrey Satellite Technology Ltd (SSTL-300)
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Workhorse configuration for modern 100-300 kg commercial satellites.

components.name: Isogrid Interplanetary Heavy Platform (ISO-DEEP-03)
components.description: Monolithic aluminum-lithium CNC isogrid cylinder with titanium load-bearing thrust cones designed to withstand heavy-lift launch acceleration.

advantages: Supports up to 1,400 kg of payload and propellant tanks
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Supports large propellant loads for deep-space and high-energy missions, at the expense of higher structural mass.

reference_source.heritage_reference: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory Mars 2020 / Europa Clipper Primary Bus
reference_source.benchmark_notes: NASA deep-space flagship structural bus standard.

components.name: Radiation-Tolerant Flash Mass Memory (FLASH-MEM-64)
components.description: NAND Flash Solid-State Recorder featuring Error-Correcting Code (ECC) and automated bad-block retirement.

disadvantages: 64 GB buffer can fill quickly during high-resolution multi-pass imaging
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Sufficient for low-rate instruments, but risks memory overflow if using high-data payloads without frequent ground passes.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Innoflight Solid-State Recorder / ESA PROBA-V Mass Memory
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Standard small-satellite solid-state recorder.

components.name: High-Throughput NVMe Space SSD (SPACE-SSD-512)
components.description: High-speed PCIe NVMe Solid-State Storage Module with triple-modular redundant (TMR) controller logic.

advantages: High write speed (1.2 Gbps) ingests multi-gigabit raw sensor streams without dropping frames
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Handles uncompressed high-resolution data streams, but adds to the thermal load and power budget.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Mercury Systems Space Solid-State Recorders / NASA PACE mission
reference_source.benchmark_notes: High-speed Earth observation mass memory standard.

components.name: Rad-Hard MRAM Deep-Space Mass Store (RAD-MRAM-2000)
components.description: Magnetoresistive RAM (MRAM) architecture immune to radiation-induced bitflips with hardware wear-leveling and a 2-terabyte capacity.

advantages: Near-zero bitflip vulnerability even in intense radiation belts
2 TB storage accommodates months of planetary observation data
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Offers deep radiation resilience and large storage for long-duration interplanetary missions, but carries a high price tag.

reference_source.heritage_reference: Everspin Rad-Hard MRAM / JPL Europa Clipper Memory Subsystem
reference_source.benchmark_notes: State-of-the-art radiation-immune planetary mass storage.

components.name: Cryo-Assay Imaging Spectrometer (CAS-20)
components.description: Shortwave infrared imaging spectrometer paired with an integrated cryo-drill sampler for volatile and astrobiological detection on icy bodies.

advantages: Direct detection of organic polymers, methane, and prebiotic ammonia complexes
disadvantages: Requires 52W continuous power and active cooling
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Unlocks primary astrobiology objectives at Titan, Europa, and Enceladus at the expense of higher power and thermal requirements.

reference_source.heritage_reference: NASA Dragonfly DraMS / Cassini VIMS Spectrometer
reference_source.benchmark_notes: Calibrated against Outer Planet astrobiology payloads.

components.name: Pu-238 Multi-Mission RTG (MMRTG-125)
components.description: Solid-state thermoelectric generator powered by plutonium-238 alpha decay heat, providing unflagging power beyond the asteroid belt.

advantages: Operates independently of solar distance (even past 50 AU)
Provides 2000W of waste heat for thermal loop management in cryogenic deep space
trade_offs.engineering_trade_off: Essential for outer planetary and deep space exploration where solar irradiance is insufficient.

reference_source.heritage_reference: JPL Curiosity / Perseverance / New Horizons MMRTG Subsystem
reference_source.benchmark_notes: DOE / NASA Glenn MMRTG flight qualification benchmark.
